findings.message: Import the bivariate prefixes from their actual module. `./constants` exports neither `LAYER_BIVARIATE_PREFIX` nor `SOURCE_BIVARIATE_PREFIX`; both are defined in `~core/logical_layers/constants`. These imports fail type checking and module loading, preventing the renderer from being used. Restore the imports from the existing module.

Keep legend thresholds in the same units as axis values. `createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes` configures max-min normalization and potentially sentiment inversion, while the copied legend steps remain raw quotient thresholds. The shared style generator compares those thresholds against `linearNormalization` results. For example, an axis with steps spanning 0–100 now supplies values between 0 and 1 against those original thresholds, assigning hexagons to incorrect color classes. Preserve raw axis calculations or transform the thresholds consistently before delegating.

`LAYER_BIVARIATE_PREFIX` and `SOURCE_BIVARIATE_PREFIX` are imported from `./constants`, but they are not defined there. They live in `~core/logical_layers/constants`. This fails type-checking, and with esbuild/Vite the values become `undefined`, so source and layer ids turn into `undefined<id>`. Every bivariate and MCDA layer would break.

`stepOverrides` passes the raw bivariate axis steps (actual quotient values such as 0, 10, 1000). However, `score` and `base` are MCDA dimensions built by `createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes` with max-min normalization, sentiment and transformation, so they produce values in 0..1. The class thresholds then don't match the normalized values, most hexes fall into one corner class, and the bivariate map shows the wrong colours. The steps need to be normalized the same way, or the raw quotient values should be classified without the MCDA scoring.

Max-zoom regression. `MultivariateRenderer.getMaxZoomLevel` reads `layer.style` from the tile source, not the converted `state.style`. For bivariate legends and the MCDA layers from `mcdaLayer.ts`, the source has no multivariate style, so maxzoom falls back to `FALLBACK_BIVARIATE_MAX_ZOOM` (9). The old code used `getMaxNumeratorZoomLevel(quotients)` and `getMaxMCDAZoomLevel(style.config)`. Layers whose indicators have different max zooms will now overzoom or underzoom tiles.

User-visible behaviour change that the refactor framing doesn't flag. Bivariate hex clicks no longer show `MapHexTooltip` (cell label, legend cell index, x/y quotient values, hex colour). They now show the multivariate/MCDA popup with normalized scores. Clicks also now dispatch the `mcda_popup` metrics event for bivariate layers, which skews analytics. This needs product sign-off or a bivariate-specific `createPopupContent`.

`createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes` throws `incorrect_axis_step_format` when an axis has no `datasetStats` and no numeric steps. That conversion now runs synchronously inside `willMount`/`willSourceUpdate`, so a malformed legend crashes the renderer hook. Previously only layer generation was affected. This path has no guard and no test.

If neither an MCDA style nor a legend is present, `convertStyle` returns null and the layer is silently not mounted. The old code threw `Vector layers must have legend`, which made the misconfiguration visible. Consider at least logging an error.

The new `MCDARenderer` is not used anywhere: `getLayerRenderer` and `mcdaLayer.ts` still instantiate `BivariateRenderer` for MCDA. It has no tests and no readme, contrary to AGENTS.md, yet it is announced as a new feature. Either wire it in with tests and docs, or remove it.

The tests mock `createDefaultMCDAConfig` and use axis steps with no `datasetStats`. They never exercise the real config, the normalization/step mismatch, or the renderers themselves, because `BivariateRenderer` and `MCDARenderer` have no tests. Coverage of the actual behaviour change (layer spec, zoom, popup) is effectively zero.

Several doc entries now point to `BivariateRenderer.tsx` lines 1–45 for 'addSource/addLayer', 'event listener registration via registerMapListener' and 'feature state logic'. The wrapper contains none of these anymore; that logic is in `ClickableFeaturesRenderer`/`MultivariateRenderer`. The references are misleading and should point to the real locations.

The replacement paragraph drops the list indentation of the surrounding numbered list, so the following items and the mapbox reference render outside the list. It also no longer explains how legend steps map to paint rules (score/base dimensions, step overrides).

`LAYER_BIVARIATE_PREFIX` and `SOURCE_BIVARIATE_PREFIX` are imported from `./constants`, but `BivariateRenderer/constants.ts` doesn't export them. They live in `~core/logical_layers/constants`, which the old code imported from. TypeScript fails to compile here, and at runtime the source and layer IDs would be `undefined` + id. The diff never touches `constants.ts`, so the build breaks.

The scales don't match, so bivariate layers get the wrong colours. `createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes` builds score/base layers with `normalization: 'max-min'`, sentiment and transformation, so `linearNormalization` produces values in the 0..1 range. But `stepOverrides` passes the legend's raw axis steps (`legend.axis.x.steps` / `legend.axis.y.steps`, in raw numerator/denominator units). `classResolver` then compares normalized values against raw borders, which puts almost every hex in the wrong class. `createStepsForMCDADimension` only uses axis steps when normalization is `'no'`, so this mapping is wrong. The unit test only checks the object shape, not that the rendered classes match the legacy `generateLayerFromLegend` output.

The sentiment/direction from `createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes` can flip an axis (`sentimentReversed`). The legacy bivariate classing used raw quotient values with no inversion. Even with correct steps, cells can end up mirrored relative to the legend's A1..C3 labels and colours. Also, `mcdaFilterSetup` adds filters on the MCDA layers that the legacy bivariate style never had, which can hide hexes the old renderer showed.

Max zoom regresses. `ClickableFeaturesRenderer.createTileSource` calls `MultivariateRenderer.getMaxZoomLevel(layer)`, which reads `layer.style` on the *source* (`state.source`), not the converted `state.style`. For bivariate and MCDA sources that isn't `'multivariate'`, so maxzoom silently falls back to `FALLBACK_BIVARIATE_MAX_ZOOM` (9). The old code used `getMaxNumeratorZoomLevel(quotients)` and `getMaxMCDAZoomLevel(config)`. Layers whose data supports higher zooms will now be overzoomed or capped.

Bivariate popups change in a way the PR doesn't present as a UX change. The `MapHexTooltip` popup (cell label, x/y quotient values, hex colour) is replaced by the generic multivariate/MCDA popup showing normalized scores. Bivariate clicks also now dispatch the `mcda_popup` metrics event, which skews analytics. If this is intended, it needs product sign-off. Otherwise keep a bivariate-specific `createPopupContent`.

With no legend and a non-MCDA style, `convertStyle` returns null. `_updateMap` then quietly skips mounting the layer and popup, but still adds the source and border layer. The old code threw `Vector layers must have legend`, so this misconfiguration is now silently hidden.

`MCDARenderer` isn't used anywhere: `getLayerRenderer` and `mcdaLayer.ts` still create `BivariateRenderer`. It's dead, untested code that copies `BivariateRenderer`'s MCDA path, and its source/layer prefixes (`mcda-source-`, `mcda-layer-`) are hard-coded strings instead of constants. Either wire it in with tests or drop it from this refactor.

`willSourceUpdate` and `willMount` are identical copies apart from the super call, and the same pattern is repeated in `MCDARenderer`. Overriding one shared hook (for example a `transformState`/`convertStyle` hook in `ClickableFeaturesRenderer`) would avoid the copies and also cover any other hooks that read `state.style`.

The tests use `toMatchObject` on the config shape only, and the MCDA test passes `layers: []`. Nothing checks the generated score/base MCDA layers or the resulting fill-colour expression, so the step/normalization mismatch above passes. The rendering parity that matters for this refactor isn't tested.

The docs now say `BivariateRenderer.tsx` lines 1–45 do event listener registration via `registerMapListener`, feature state logic and addSource/addLayer. That file no longer does any of these; it all lives in `ClickableFeaturesRenderer`/`MultivariateRenderer`. The references should point there instead.

The new lines drop the list indentation used by the surrounding numbered items, which breaks the readme's list structure. They also say the style is created with 'proper style rules for every legend step', which isn't true given the normalized-vs-raw step mismatch.
